identity.standaloneProfile: Public GitHub Pages uses cryptographically signed access permits plus signed access configuration and revocation data. Browser state does not create administrator authority by itself.
identity.schoolProfile: The prepared school profile uses server-session identity and disables local provider keys. Live school-runtime authorization evidence remains deferred until an approved deployment exists.
identity.session: Permit claims, role, application scope, training state, time bounds and revocation are validated fail-closed. Shared-device end-work clears credential/session state and rotates session-generation tombstones.

requestApiAi.controls: AI Studio does not originate provider AI operations. It distributes a versioned immutable AI Core whose provider-facing behavior is governed by the consuming application and the AI Core contract; adding a Studio AI operation requires inventory, policy and regression updates.

egress.standalone: Studio network activity is constrained to same-origin resources and the configured GitHub Pages ecosystem origin used for application registry and launch flows.
egress.school: The prepared school profile is same-origin oriented. Runtime network enforcement and central gateway evidence remain deferred with the school-server phase.
egress.crossApp: Cross-application navigation, registry synchronization and handoff use allowlisted application identities and bounded contracts; arbitrary provider destinations are not a Studio UI capability.

files.currentBoundary: Material and handoff imports are parsed through bounded application contracts. Artifact envelopes use SHA-256 verification, material fields have size limits, and exports require explicit user action.
files.serverBoundary: Server-side quarantine and host filesystem isolation remain runtime controls to verify only after the school-server phase is approved.

dataLifecycle.classification: Application content may contain student or teacher material; administrative records and signed access state can contain personal or security-relevant metadata. Telemetry is configured as non-content.
dataLifecycle.storage: Owned data is namespaced across localStorage, sessionStorage and Cache Storage. Cross-application namespaces are explicit exceptions and the suite-session tombstone is reserved shared platform state.
dataLifecycle.retention: Shared-device end-work and explicit deletion execute manifest-driven cleanup with verification; transient handoff state is bounded and access credentials are cleared on session end.

release.promotion: candidate -> cumulative P5 and GARP 2.7 FOUNDATION gates -> canonical pull request -> protected main -> exact release identity -> verified GitHub Pages deployment
release.publicAssurance: GARP 2.7 FOUNDATION is the active security contract. GARP 2.5.1 remains a regression baseline; production signing remains transitional and school-runtime SHIELD-LIVE controls remain NOT_TESTED.

inventory.changeRule: Any new Studio AI operation, egress destination, import class, storage class, privileged capability, cross-application authority or release authority requires inventory update plus positive and negative regression coverage.

securityHealth.localCi: Reference package and contract selftests, semantic policy admission, architecture-integrity, application boundary mutations, auto-patch contract checks, P5 and retained GARP 2.5.1 regressions form the local release gate.
securityHealth.live: School-runtime protection health remains NOT_TESTED until an approved target environment provides trusted runtime evidence.
securityHealth.failureMode: Missing, stale, mismatched, parser-error or empty critical evidence never becomes PASS.

incident.current: Fail-closed access verification, revocation handling, shared-device cleanup, bounded imports, exact release evidence, Safe Promotion and rollback-aware update controls form the current application-side response baseline.
incident.future: Central alert delivery, infrastructure containment and school-runtime incident actions require the separately approved server phase.

recovery.current: Release integrity, protected promotion, service-worker update deferral, last-known-good signed access configuration, shared-device cleanup and rollback-aware release workflows form the current recovery baseline.
recovery.future: Server restore, trust-root custody, live egress containment and runtime recovery drills remain NOT_TESTED until the school environment is approved.
